headline: Willson Contreras Powers Red Sox To Big Victory Over Rival Yankees
morning_brew: There is nothing better than going into the Bronx and shoving a victory right down their throats. Friday night was a beautiful sight as the Sox took down the Yankees by a score of five to three. Willson Contreras was the absolute star of the show, blasting a home run and driving in three runs to pace the offense. Sonny Gray was gutsy on the mound, grinding through six and a third innings to pick up the win despite giving up eight hits.

Danny Coulombe and Justin Slaten did their jobs out of the bullpen to set the stage for the ninth inning. Then came Aroldis Chapman, who decided to give us all a collective heart attack by walking two batters in the final frame. He locked it down for the save, but my blood pressure does not need that kind of drama in June. Still, taking the opening game of this series in New York is massive for a club that has struggled to find consistency on the road.

This win gives us a little breathing room at twenty-seven and thirty-five, but we are still in the basement of the AL East. We have another battle tonight in New York, and we need the bats to stay hot. The Celtics and Bruins are done for the year, so all eyes in the Hub are on the local nine to keep this momentum going. Let's see if we can secure a series win against our biggest rivals before we head down to Tampa.
